prelaunch_alignment: These exact seal, invalid-close, stopped-stage enumeration, S80 bracketing, and pre-create state-machine corrections remain protocol revision .3 because revision .3 has never been sealed or launched and no counted subject task or model call has occurred under it.
title: Three-configuration first-attempt causal semantic simulation with controller-custodied sandbox repair
purpose: Test whether exact predecessor bytes causally constrain a bounded two-topic synthesis, audit, repair, integration, specialist reduction, sandbox write, and final re-audit chain.

authority.canonical: The frozen fixture captures canonical owner prose at snapshot time for fixture-scoped semantics only; it has no current-Plans, product, production, release, or readiness authority.
authority.lineage_only: The frozen v2 ledger registry and four selected frozen ledger state projections may support snapshot provenance, frozen planning history, alternatives, corrections, and unresolved candidates, but never independently create normative product truth.
authority.instruction_scope: The request authorizes this bounded test only and does not amend live Plans, promote the throwaway fixture, or authorize compilation, WorkNodes, implementation, build, or release.

configuration_isolation.route_lock: The controller permanently binds each slot to the exact model and reasoning effort it requests before launch; substitution, fallback, relabeling, or cross-slot reuse in controller records is INVALID. Platform-returned task, thread, host, and route metadata are preserved as observations, not independent attestation of the hidden serving snapshot.
configuration_isolation.freshness: Every subject stage is requested as one new projectless task. Platform-returned new task, thread, and host identifiers plus reopened final-item, tool-item, delegation, and user-input-request counts are the observable freshness evidence; they do not reveal or freeze the hidden system stack.
configuration_isolation.identical_stage_inputs: For each stage, original template bytes and every frozen source or role-contract byte are identical across configurations. Only actual same-slot predecessor artifacts, receipts, and slot-specific S80 custody observations may differ.
configuration_isolation.specialist_byte_identity: Within a slot, S60P, S60C, and S60K receive one identical specialist-packet byte sequence; only their fixed role templates differ.

deterministic_transforms.operation: Validate the exact passing S10A artifact, replace only the scorer-key-selected Topic A decision with the deterministic authority fault, retain clean controls, and bind the S10A payload hash.
Validate the exact passing S10B artifact, replace only the scorer-key-selected Topic B decision with the deterministic qualifier fault, retain clean controls, and bind the S10B payload hash.

Validate exact S20A, S30A, and S40A bindings, finding identifiers, bounded patch index, and test/replace pair; apply the actual guarded S40A patch deterministically and emit the repaired Topic A artifact.

Validate exact S20B, S30B, and S40B bindings, finding identifiers, bounded patch index, and test/replace pair; apply the actual guarded S40B patch deterministically and emit the repaired Topic B artifact.
Validate the exact passing S50 artifact and append only the scorer-key-selected unsupported I-E99 cross-topic edge while preserving the supported-edge clean controls and binding the S50 payload hash.

Validate exact S50, S55, and S70 bindings and the exact guarded test/remove pair; apply the actual reducer patch deterministically, remove only I-E99, preserve supported edges, and emit S50-equivalent content with S80 identity and predecessor hashes.

causal_handoff_contract.raw_artifacts: Every model-visible dynamic predecessor is the exact immutable UTF-8 JSON payload captured from that same slot, embedded with its SHA-256 and, where declared by the fixed template, payload byte count. Summaries, regenerated objects, oracle copies, and cross-slot artifacts are forbidden substitutes.
causal_handoff_contract.direct_consumption: Audits verdict actual predecessor decision identifiers; repair proposals contain test operations against actual predecessor values; deterministic repair stages apply the actual proposals; integration names actual repaired topic hashes; specialists inspect actual S55 bytes; the reducer dispositions actual specialist finding identifiers; S90 receives and re-audits every actual stage artifact.
causal_handoff_contract.capture_storage: A subject payload is canonical minified UTF-8 JSON with no terminal line ending. Its run-record storage is those exact bytes plus exactly one LF; payload and storage hashes are distinct and preserved.
causal_handoff_contract.immutability: Attempt-one bytes, call receipt, packet, model route, task identity, and normalized paths are write-once evidence. Parsing or scoring never normalizes or edits captured bytes.
causal_handoff_contract.receipt_binding: Every ordinary subject call receipt binds protocol, slot, stage, reservation, attempt-start, controller-requested model and reasoning effort, platform-returned task, thread, and host metadata, any platform-returned route observation, reopened final-item and activity observations, exact rendered packet payload and storage, exact raw capture payload and storage, normalized paths, and ordered input bindings. Every nonempty final output, including prose refusal or output accompanied by tool, delegation, or user-input activity, is preserved in a normal raw capture and call receipt and mechanically scored FAIL when it differs from the exact expected canonical JSON or has prohibited activity. Subject failure receipt is permitted only when no nonempty final bytes exist. Replay across stages or slots is INVALID; platform-returned fields are observations and the receipt does not independently attest the requested route or any unexposed serving state.
causal_handoff_contract.S90_expansion: S90 receives each unique S10A-through-S80 payload once in stage order rather than recursive envelopes, plus lineage metadata and the three raw S80 custody artifacts. This bounds prompt growth while exposing the complete causal chain.

fault_injections.S20A: one structurally valid authority promotion that treats lineage-only ledger state as normative
fault_injections.S20B: one structurally valid canonical qualifier or exception inversion attached to a real but semantically non-supporting citation
fault_injections.S55: one structurally valid unsupported cross-topic edge I-E99 between real identifiers
fault_injections.clean_controls: Source-supported adjacent decisions and cross-topic edges remain present; blanket rejection or deletion fails exact scoring.
fault_injections.determinism: Fault targets, replacement values, and array locations are frozen in scorer_key.json before launch and are never disclosed to subject prompts.

lockstep_waves.advance: all three controller-requested routes, the sealed receipt binding, immutable-file custody, and source-currentness check must pass before any W10 dispatch or subject call
the only operation that may issue terminal configuration and cohort statuses

lockstep_rule: No configuration advances to a later wave while another still-active configuration has not completed or been stopped in the current wave. Parallel siblings inside W10, W20, W30, W40, and W60 may run concurrently, but the next wave waits for the complete cohort-wave disposition recorded in the controller wave ledger.

cohort_wave_ledger.purpose: Controller-custodied proof that cohort waves were authorized, dispatched, completed, and stopped in the fixed order without relying on task timestamps or reconstructed narrative.
cohort_wave_ledger.separate_gates: W00 preseal, seal, and launch-currentness admission is separately evidenced by its canonical gate receipts and is not a runtime ledger event. W99 source close and cohort close is separately evidenced by close-source and cohort-close receipts and is not a runtime ledger event. This avoids circularly placing the close that consumes the ledger inside the ledger itself.

types_and_literals.kind: string enum SUBJECT, DETERMINISTIC, DETERMINISTIC_AND_CONTROLLER_WRITE matching wave_registry
types_and_literals.prior_completion_event_sha256: null for W10, otherwise lowercase 64-hex string
types_and_literals.dispatch_set: array of one or more dispatch items

dispatch_event.construction: Before creating any subject task or executing any deterministic runtime stage in the wave, the controller apply_patch-creates this absent canonical event. dispatch_set is ordered by slot-alpha, slot-bravo, slot-charlie and then by the fixed stage order within the wave, omitting stopped slots. task_id and thread_id are null because no task may exist yet; they remain null for deterministic cells. status is DISPATCH_RECORDED.
dispatch_event.exact_active_cross_product: Derive active slots only from the fully semantically validated contiguous prior completion chain, beginning with all three slots and removing a slot after its first validated subject FAIL. For a reached wave with at least one active slot, dispatch_set must equal the complete slot-major Cartesian product of those active slots in slot-alpha, slot-bravo, slot-charlie order and every registered stage for that wave in wave_registry order. No active slot, registered stage, or parallel sibling may be omitted; no stopped slot, duplicate, extra stage, subset, invented cell, or reordered item is valid. A wave with no active slots has no dispatch event.
dispatch_event.chain: W10 prior_completion_event_sha256 is null. Every later reached dispatch event binds the exact immediately preceding reached completion-event payload hash, including waves after one or more configurations were stopped for subject FAIL.
dispatch_event.serialization_and_hash: The file is exact canonical minified UTF-8 JSON payload plus one storage LF. dispatch_event_sha256 is SHA-256 over payload bytes only after removing exactly that LF.
dispatch_event.no_permission_without_event: No task creation, model call, deterministic transform, or S80 write may start unless the exact matching immutable current-wave dispatch event exists and passes intrinsic current-dispatch validation. Final wave-check is retrospective and is not required before the first cell of a newly dispatched wave.

types_and_literals.wave_id: string registered runtime wave matching its dispatch event
types_and_literals.kind: string enum SUBJECT, DETERMINISTIC, DETERMINISTIC_AND_CONTROLLER_WRITE matching dispatch and wave_registry
types_and_literals.completion_set: nonempty array with exact dispatch_set cardinality and order
types_and_literals.completion_item.status: string enum PASS, FAIL, INVALID; FAIL allowed only for subject
types_and_literals.completion_item.artifact_payload_sha256: lowercase 64-hex string for PASS and for ordinary scored-capture FAIL, null for subject-failure-receipt FAIL or INVALID
types_and_literals.completion_item.call_receipt_sha256: lowercase 64-hex string for subject PASS and ordinary scored-capture FAIL, null for subject-failure-receipt FAIL, deterministic, or INVALID
types_and_literals.completion_item.task_id: nonempty string for subject PASS or FAIL, null otherwise
types_and_literals.completion_item.thread_id: nonempty string for subject PASS or FAIL, null otherwise
types_and_literals.completion_item.attempt_start_receipt_sh: lowercase 64-hex string for a created subject task, null for deterministic, pre-ID TASK_CREATION_ERROR, or INVALID
types_and_literals.completion_item.subject_failure_receipt_: lowercase 64-hex string for subject-failure-receipt FAIL, null otherwise
types_and_literals.completion_item.controller_invalid_recei: lowercase 64-hex string for INVALID, null otherwise

completion_event.construction: After every dispatched cell has a first-attempt disposition, the controller apply_patch-creates this absent canonical event. completion_set has exactly one entry for each dispatch_set entry in the same order and no entry for an undispatched cell.
completion_event.subject_binding: For a PASS or ordinary scored-capture FAIL subject cell, task_id, thread_id, attempt_start_receipt_sha256, artifact_payload_sha256, and call_receipt_sha256 are non-null and must equal the reopened attempt-start, task evidence, capture, and canonical call receipt; subject_failure_receipt_sha256 and controller_invalid_receipt_sha256 are null.
completion_event.subject_failure_binding: For a trustworthy subject behavior or transport FAIL with no nonempty final bytes, artifact_payload_sha256 and call_receipt_sha256 are null, subject_failure_receipt_sha256 binds the canonical subject failure receipt, and controller_invalid_receipt_sha256 is null. task_id, thread_id, and attempt_start_receipt_sha256 are non-null after successful task creation; all three are null only for a pre-ID TASK_CREATION_ERROR bound to the reservation.
completion_event.deterministic_binding: For a PASS deterministic cell, task_id, thread_id, attempt_start_receipt_sha256, call_receipt_sha256, subject_failure_receipt_sha256, and controller_invalid_receipt_sha256 are null; artifact_payload_sha256 binds its canonical controller artifact.
completion_event.invalid_binding: For an INVALID cell, artifact_payload_sha256, call_receipt_sha256, task_id, thread_id, attempt_start_receipt_sha256, and subject_failure_receipt_sha256 are null, and controller_invalid_receipt_sha256 is the exact canonical controller-invalid receipt payload hash. Any returned task or thread metadata relevant to the invalidity is evidence bound by the controller-invalid receipt, not trusted completion identity.
completion_event.wave_status: status is PASS when all completion cells pass, SUBJECT_FAIL when one or more subject cells fail without controller invalidity, and INVALID when a canonical controller-invalid receipt exists.
completion_event.serialization_and_hash: The file is exact canonical minified UTF-8 JSON payload plus one storage LF. completion_event_sha256 is SHA-256 over payload bytes only after removing exactly that LF.

parallel_sibling_rule.rule: The dispatch event may authorize all same-slot siblings in that parallel wave before any one sibling result exists. If one sibling later FAILs, every sibling already present in that immutable dispatch_set may finish and its first-attempt result is retained in the completion event. The controller creates no additional task for that stopped slot and excludes the slot from every later dispatch_set.

cohort_wave_ledger.global_identity_uniqueness: Across every completion event, ordinary call receipt, and subject failure receipt, every non-null task_id is globally unique and every non-null thread_id is globally unique across all slots and subject stages. A repeated task or thread identity, even with different slot or stage labels, is custody INVALID for the entire cohort.

types_and_literals.launch_source_receipt_sha256: lowercase 64-hex string equal to every event binding
types_and_literals.waves: array containing the contiguous reached prefix of runtime_wave_order; empty only when W00 invalidity prevented W10 dispatch
types_and_literals.wave_item.wave_id: string at the corresponding runtime_wave_order position
types_and_literals.wave_item.status: string enum PASS, SUBJECT_FAIL, INVALID matching completion event

index.construction: After W90 completes, immediately after an earlier cohort INVALID stops runtime execution, or immediately after a subject-fail wave leaves no active slots, the controller apply_patch-creates one absent canonical index over every reached runtime wave in fixed order. It never edits or replaces an event file. For an early terminal, no later wave files may exist; an INVALID terminal requires final status INVALID, while an all-slots-stopped subject terminal requires final status SUBJECT_FAIL.
index.hash_definition: cohort_wave_index.json is exact canonical minified UTF-8 JSON payload plus one storage LF. cohort_wave_ledger_sha256 is SHA-256 over payload bytes only after removing exactly that LF.
index.immutability: Dispatch events, completion events, and the final index are create-once apply_patch artifacts. Overwrite, append, in-place update, reserialization, deletion, cleanup, or alternate index is INVALID.

wave_check.failure: Any defect is cohort custody INVALID rather than a subject FAIL.

current_dispatch_admission.required_argument: Every operational command for a runtime cell takes the exact normalized path to that cell's current immutable dispatch event as --wave-dispatch-receipt.
current_dispatch_admission.controller_invalid_latch: Before trusting a current dispatch and before every cell action, enumerate runs/cohort/controller_invalid/ without trusting the prior completion chain. The directory must be absent or an empty regular nonlink directory. Any entry, including a canonical receipt not yet referenced by a completion, permanently latches cohort INVALID and rejects dispatch admission; a malformed, duplicate, nonregular, symlink, unknown-wave, or wrong-protocol entry is itself CUSTODY INVALID. No current or later dispatch may convert an existing invalid receipt back into an active cohort.
current_dispatch_admission.subject_precreation_state_machine: For a dispatched subject cell the only permitted packet-dependent evidence before reservation is the exact admitted runs/<slot>/packets/<stage>.txt. Render requires reservation, creation metadata, attempt-start, post-task metadata, capture, call receipt, subject-failure receipt, and completion all absent before it stores the packet. Reservation reopens that packet and again requires runs/<slot>/attempts/<stage>.reservation.json, runs/<slot>/platform/<stage>.creation.json, runs/<slot>/attempts/<stage>.start.json, runs/<slot>/platform/<stage>.json, runs/<slot>/captures/<stage>.json, runs/<slot>/receipts/<stage>.json, runs/<slot>/subject_failures/<stage>.json, and the wave completion all absent before creating the reservation. Only after the reservation is stored and reopened may create_thread occur. A preexisting creation or post-task metadata file can never be retroactively legitimized by a later reservation.
current_dispatch_admission.temporal_rule: The controller apply_patch-stores and intrinsically validates the dispatch event before creating any same-wave task or running any same-wave deterministic operation. The exact current dispatch receipt and the controller-invalid latch are revalidated for the selected cell before each render, reservation, task creation, model call, score, deterministic transform, or S80 write-related operation. After dispatch storage, only cells already listed in its dispatch_set may be created or executed. The final wave-check later reopens the entire immutable event chain and index for retrospective cohort validation.
current_dispatch_admission.failure: Missing, wrong, malformed, stale, cross-wave, cross-slot, or intrinsically invalid dispatch receipt is BINDING or CUSTODY cohort INVALID; it never becomes subject FAIL.

types.payload_sha256: lowercase 64-hex SHA-256 over canonical payload bytes excluding one storage LF
types.payload_bytes: nonnegative integer exact payload byte count
types.storage_sha256: lowercase 64-hex SHA-256 over payload plus exactly one LF

types_and_literals.dispatch_event_sha256: lowercase 64-hex exact current dispatch payload hash
types_and_literals.rendered_packet_payload_sha256: lowercase 64-hex exact admitted rendered packet payload hash

reservation.timing: After intrinsic current-dispatch admission and deterministic packet rendering, but immediately before create_thread, the controller reopens the exact admitted packet, proves the complete precreation evidence set pristine, apply_patch-creates this absent canonical reservation, and reopens it for exact validation.
reservation.exclusivity: At reservation creation the packet is the only permitted existing packet-dependent cell evidence. If this reservation, platform creation metadata, attempt-start, post-task platform metadata, capture, call receipt, subject failure receipt, or completion for the cell already exists, reservation and create_thread are prohibited and the cohort is CUSTODY INVALID. No reservation may be replaced, deleted, reused, or created after any task evidence.

result_rules.CREATED: result is CREATED; task_id, thread_id, and host_id are nonempty strings; error_type and error_message are null
result_rules.ERROR: result is ERROR; task_id, thread_id, and host_id are null; error_type and error_message are nonempty strings

platform_creation_metadata.request_rules: requested_model and requested_thinking exactly match the sealed slot route; projectless is true; rendered_packet_payload_sha256 matches the reservation.
platform_creation_metadata.serialization: Canonical minified UTF-8 payload plus exactly one storage LF; the creation payload hash excludes that LF. The controller apply_patch-creates this absent file immediately from the create_thread result before any wait or final read.

types_and_literals.dispatch_event_sha256: lowercase 64-hex matching reservation and current dispatch
types_and_literals.rendered_packet_payload_sha256: lowercase 64-hex matching reservation and exact task input
types_and_literals.platform_creation_metadata_payload_sha25: lowercase 64-hex exact payload hash of runs/<slot>/platform/<stage>.creation.json whose result is CREATED

attempt_start.timing: Immediately after create_thread returns trustworthy task, thread, host, and creation metadata, and before wait_threads, read_thread, final inspection, capture, call receipt, failure receipt, or scoring, the controller apply_patch-creates this absent attempt-start and reopens it for exact validation.
attempt_start.binding: Attempt-start binds the one reservation, exact dispatch, rendered packet, controller-requested route, and creation observation. No waiting or final read is permitted before it exists.
attempt_start.task_creation_failure: If creation metadata result is ERROR, the reservation remains and no attempt-start exists. That exact creation metadata may support TASK_CREATION_ERROR subject failure with null identities; missing, malformed, or untrustworthy creation evidence is cohort INVALID. No second reservation or create_thread attempt is allowed.

ordinary_call_receipt_attempt_binding.placement: Immediately after host_id, fields are attempt_reservation, attempt_start, platform_creation_metadata, then platform_metadata in that exact order.
ordinary_call_receipt_attempt_binding.attempt_reservation: non-null object with exact standard_receipt_binding keys for runs/<slot>/attempts/<stage>.reservation.json
ordinary_call_receipt_attempt_binding.attempt_start: non-null object with exact standard_receipt_binding keys for runs/<slot>/attempts/<stage>.start.json
ordinary_call_receipt_attempt_binding.platform_creation_metadata: non-null object with exact standard_receipt_binding keys for runs/<slot>/platform/<stage>.creation.json whose result is CREATED
ordinary_call_receipt_attempt_binding.platform_metadata: non-null object with exact standard_receipt_binding keys for the canonical reopened post-task platform metadata; it is distinct from creation metadata
ordinary_call_receipt_attempt_binding.validation: All four nested bindings are exact byte and path bindings, not hash-only aliases. The call receipt reopens them, requires their cell, dispatch, packet, reservation-to-start, creation result, task, thread, and host bindings, and rejects any missing, extra, reordered, or mismatched field.
ordinary_call_receipt_attempt_binding.nonempty_capture_precondition: An ordinary capture and call receipt are permitted only when reopened platform metadata reports final_output_bytes greater than zero, final_output_sha256 equals the exact nonempty captured payload hash, and capture storage equals those nonempty payload bytes plus one LF. A zero-byte payload, an LF-only capture storage file, final_output_bytes equal to zero, or null final_output_sha256 is forbidden on the ordinary path and must route to the exclusive subject-failure-receipt path when metadata is trustworthy.

cohort_wave_ledger.manifest_binding: Every configuration result manifest contains the exact field cohort_wave_ledger_sha256 immediately after launch_source_receipt_sha256, equal to the final index payload hash. Cohort close reopens the index, reruns wave-check, requires all three manifests to bind that same hash, and contains the same field cohort_wave_ledger_sha256 immediately after close_source_receipt_sha256 in its canonical output.
cohort_wave_ledger.result_manifest_binding: Every normal valid-cohort configuration result manifest contains controller_invalid_receipt_sha256 immediately after cohort_wave_ledger_sha256 and its value is null. W00 or W99 INVALID uses controller_invalid_close config_results instead of constructing or rewriting normal configuration manifests.
cohort_wave_ledger.result_stage_binding: Every normal configuration result-manifest stage row contains subject_failure_receipt_sha256 after call_receipt_sha256 and controller_invalid_receipt_sha256 after subject_failure_receipt_sha256. Exactly one of these shapes is valid: PASS binds artifact and, for subjects, call receipt; ordinary scored-capture FAIL binds artifact and call receipt; subject-behavior-or-transport FAIL binds only subject_failure_receipt_sha256; skip binds none. controller_invalid_receipt_sha256 is null on the normal manifest path because any INVALID uses controller_invalid_close.

attempt_policy.first_attempt_scoring: Any nonempty final bytes are captured exactly once and scored mechanically. PASS requires exact byte equality to the dynamically recomputed canonical expected JSON plus zero prohibited tool, delegation, and user-input activity. All other nonempty output, including prose refusal, invalid JSON, wrong schema or key order, wrong semantics, truncation, or output accompanied by prohibited activity, is ordinary scored-capture FAIL. REFUSAL is not a no-capture failure kind and has no semantic detector: its raw bytes fail only by the same frozen exact-byte, JSON, and activity rules. Zero final bytes are never an ordinary capture: with trustworthy metadata, timeout, task error, empty output, no output, or prohibited activity without final bytes uses the exclusive subject failure receipt and no capture/call receipt exists. Route mismatch, untrustworthy or missing metadata, packet mismatch, identity ambiguity, replay, or custody defect is cohort INVALID.

TASK_CREATION_ERROR binds result ERROR with null IDs no attempt-start and no post-task metadata

subject_failure_receipt.attempt_binding_validation: Immediately after host_id, fields are attempt_reservation, attempt_start, platform_creation_metadata, then platform_metadata in that exact order. Each non-null object uses the exact path, payload hash and bytes, and storage hash and bytes schema used by ordinary call receipts. The controller reopens and validates them; hash-only shorthand, wrong ordering, missing fields, or an attempt-start on creation result ERROR is invalid.
subject_failure_receipt.classification: Only zero-byte outcomes qualify. TASK_CREATION_ERROR, prohibited activity without final bytes, timeout, task error, empty final output, or no final output is first-attempt subject FAIL when every applicable trust precondition passes. The controller apply_patch-creates this receipt instead of a capture and call receipt. Any nonempty final bytes must be captured and mechanically scored through the ordinary path. Zero-byte payload creation, LF-only capture storage, or an ordinary call receipt with final_output_bytes zero is prohibited and becomes CUSTODY INVALID rather than an alternate encoding of this FAIL. The first applicable failure_kind in the listed enum precedence is used.
subject_failure_receipt.invalid_boundary: Missing, malformed, contradictory, or untrustworthy platform metadata; route mismatch; packet mismatch; task, thread, or host ambiguity; identity replay; wrong dispatch; or any custody defect prevents this receipt and requires canonical cohort INVALID evidence.

sealed_preflight_gate.ordering: The controller first captures and apply_patch-stores the preseal launch-source receipt, then builds a launch manifest that binds that exact receipt, then stores detached custody for the manifest. Only after those preparation writes may sealed preflight run.

launch_manifest_schema.serialization: Exact canonical minified UTF-8 JSON payload plus exactly one LF; payload hash and bytes exclude that LF and storage hash and bytes include it.

detached_custody_schema.serialization: Exact canonical minified UTF-8 JSON payload plus exactly one LF. The four manifest identity fields are recomputed from the exact launch_manifest.json payload and storage bytes; the detached file is not self-inventoried.

launch_source_receipt_contract.serialization: Exact canonical minified UTF-8 JSON payload plus exactly one LF. source_custody_sha256 is lowercase SHA-256 over the exact complete source_custody.json storage bytes including its terminal LF; it is not a payload hash with that LF removed.

immutable_inventory.ordering: immutable_files is strictly sorted by path as Unicode code-point/UTF-8 byte lexicographic order; duplicate, missing, extra, absolute, dot-segment, backslash, symlink, nonregular, or escaping paths are INVALID.
immutable_inventory.coverage: Exactly eleven root control/capsule/binding files, twelve subject templates, seventeen oracle baselines, and the canonical launch-source receipt. launch_manifest.json and detached custody are excluded to avoid self-reference. No other file may be treated as immutable seal input.

sealed_preflight_gate.oracle_recomputation: Execute constructors in exact frozen file order S10A, S10B, S20A, S20B, S30A, S30B, S40A, S40B, S45A, S45B, S50, S55, S60C, S60K, S60P, S70, S80 over the frozen capsules, scorer key, integration contract, specialist packet template, role templates, schemas, and independently recomputed predecessor bytes. C, K, P is the required oracle execution/storage order; when constructing S70, explicitly select the already recomputed specialist payloads and pass/content-bind them in semantic order P, C, K so S70 specialist_artifact_hashes and dispositions remain provenance, constraint_authority, counterfactual_dependency. Never use list insertion order or oracle-file order as the S70 semantic role order, and never load an oracle file as a constructor input. Require each oracle file to be the exact canonical minified JSON payload plus one storage LF, remove exactly that LF, canonically serialize each independently recomputed object without a terminal LF, and require exact byte equality to the oracle payload bytes. A sealed storage-hash match without this recomputation is insufficient. These files remain nonoperative at runtime after launch.
sealed_preflight_gate.algorithm: If both seal artifacts are absent report UNSEALED; if exactly one exists report INVALID. Otherwise reopen launch_manifest.json, require its exact canonical storage, schema, top-level key order, literals, nested key orders, exact configs, and exact 41-row sorted immutable path list. For each row reopen the named file beneath this revision root as a regular nonlink through nonlink ancestors and compare exact storage bytes and SHA-256. Reopen fixture_binding_manifest.json and source_checks/launch.json independently, require the frozen provenance and fixture-control bindings plus the exact source receipt, then require the manifest nested launch_source_receipt object to equal its normalized path and exact payload/storage identity. Independently recompute and byte-compare all seventeen oracle baselines without reading an oracle as constructor input. Finally reopen detached custody at its fixed sibling path, require its exact canonical schema/key order/literals, and require its four manifest identity values to equal the exact manifest bytes just reopened. Mutable live Plans are never consulted. No manifest field, detached assertion, sealed oracle hash, or hash alias may substitute for reopening and recomputing the underlying frozen-fixture contract.
sealed_preflight_gate.unsealed_mode: Preparation may report UNSEALED only when both seal artifacts are absent. UNSEALED or partial seal permits no counted subject calls.
sealed_preflight_gate.failure: INVALID cohort before subject calls through the seal-independent W00 controller-invalid-close path

launch_source_gate.timing: The source observation and canonical launch receipt are created in preseal preparation before the launch manifest. Sealed preflight subsequently reopens the manifest-bound receipt and rechecks source currentness before W10.

precedence_exact: frozen canonical owner prose controls fixture-scoped product semantics only

oracle_artifacts.allowed_use: Before launch only, sealed baseline files are comparison targets for the mandatory independent deterministic recomputation of all seventeen expected artifacts. Hash inventory alone is not self-consistency evidence.
oracle_artifacts.runtime_rule: Runtime expected artifacts are recomputed from the frozen scorer key, frozen source and role-contract bytes, and the actual validated same-slot predecessors. oracle_artifacts.S90: No static S90 baseline is operative; its expected payload is recomputed from the actual complete runtime chain and validated S80 custody artifacts for that slot.

S80_write_protocol.target_existence_rule: A target is created if and only if its same-slot S80 deterministic stage reached PASS in W80. A slot stopped before PASS S80 has no slot directory, target, S80 pre-observation, global-pre observation, apply trace, write receipt, or global-post guard. Final sandbox validation expects exactly the allowlisted targets for the subset of slots with PASS S80 and no target or S80 custody file for every other slot.
S80_write_protocol.isolation: Each slot directory and target must be absent at its pre-observation. A slot write contains only that slot's actual S80 canonical payload plus exactly one storage LF and never reads or changes another slot's target.
S80_write_protocol.apply: The controller performs one apply_patch add-file operation at the exact allowlisted absent target only after the S80 pre and global-pre records exist and validate. It then records the exact apply-patch trace with the required causal bindings. Shell redirection, cp, mv, Python writes, subject writes, overwrite, retry, delete, and cleanup are prohibited.
S80_write_protocol.controller_global_cross_slot_guard: The global-pre observation is a before-write snapshot over every sandbox path outside the selected slot and binds the selected S80 pre and S80 payload. The global-post guard is emitted only after the write receipt, binds every preceding custody record including that receipt, recomputes the same outside-selected manifest, and requires exact equality. This acyclic chain proves the global observations bracket the selected write. These records are cohort custody evidence, not part of the fixed-shape raw S80 pre-observation supplied to S90; raw other-slot manifests are never embedded in an S90 packet.

S90_audit_contract.subject_terminal_field: S90 terminal is a bounded audit finding and remains provisional evidence; it cannot terminalize the configuration or cohort before W99.

failure_and_invalidation.subject_fail: After a configuration's first reached subject FAIL, preserve its ordinary scored capture and call receipt or its canonical subject failure receipt plus all custody evidence, stop that configuration immediately, mark every not-yet-started transitive stage SKIPPED_AFTER_SUBJECT_FAIL, and make no further subject calls for that configuration. Other valid configurations continue in lockstep waves.

No undispatched sibling, additional task, retry, or later-wave cell begins for that configuration.
failure_and_invalidation.deterministic_subject_dependency_fail: A deterministic transform mismatch caused by a well-custodied failing subject artifact remains part of the stopped configuration's FAIL lineage; the controller must not repair or substitute it.

controller_gate_observation.construction: The caller supplies only wave_id, invalid_class, gate_code, and a path selector when the selected table row has a variable path domain. The controller derives expected_state, expected payload/storage identity, the exact row set, and allowed path from the normative table and current trustworthy bindings; caller-supplied expected values are impossible and rejected. It performs no-follow lexical lstat observations for the table-required sorted unique normalized repository-relative paths and emits canonical bytes only; the controller apply_patch-creates the absent observation file. Expected payload fields are non-null only for MATCH_BOUND_PAYLOAD, except expected_payload_bytes may be null when W10 preserves only the hash. Expected storage fields are non-null only for MATCH_BOUND_STORAGE. lstat_mode is an exact nonnegative integer for an existing lstat result and null for ABSENT or RESOLUTION_ERROR. Symlink fields are non-null only for SYMLINK and cover raw readlink bytes without following it. Storage fields are non-null only for REGULAR_NONLINK. For a regular file with exact one-LF canonical receipt storage, payload fields cover bytes excluding that LF; otherwise payload fields are null. error_type is a stable exception-class string only for RESOLUTION_ERROR. defect_kind is derived exactly from expected versus observed state/payload/storage. At least one row must violate the normative expectation; status is INVALID_STATE_OBSERVED.
controller_gate_observation.mandatory_use: For every table-admitted path, MISSING, SYMLINK, NONREGULAR, RESOLUTION_ERROR, UNEXPECTED_PRESENCE, and STORAGE_DRIFT can be represented only by this canonical observation and require it as a controller-invalid receipt evidence path. protocol.json, r4_harness.py, and schemas.json are deliberately not table-admitted static-drift paths: any mismatch in those three is handled only by external_controller_self_hosting_fail_stop, produces no controller observation/receipt/W99 close, and grants no empirical credit.
controller_gate_observation.negative_evidence_rule: The observation is rejected if gate_code, wave, invalid_class, path domain, derived expectation, row cardinality/order, current state, defect_kind, or semantic relevance differs from the normative table. An unrelated regular file, caller-invented expectation, receipt evidence list, prose, or defective object's own claims cannot substitute for it or expand runtime authority.

controller_invalid_receipt.runtime_slot_stage_rule: For W00 or W99, slot and stage are both null. For a runtime wave they are both non-null only when an intrinsically valid exact frontier dispatch exists and the defective object belongs to that exact dispatched cell; they must equal one dispatch item. If the dispatch is missing, nonregular, malformed, semantically invalid, has the wrong wave/stages, or is not the exact active-slot cross-product, it grants zero cells and slot and stage are both null. A wave-level completion/index defect also uses null slot and stage unless the exact defective object is an individually dispatched cell artifact.
controller_invalid_receipt.rule: On the first controller, custody, route, binding, source, seal, or filesystem INVALID observation for a protocol-admitted internally terminalizable path, the controller apply_patch-creates this canonical receipt with exact normalized evidence paths and corresponding ordered payload hashes, then stops every slot. status is COHORT_INVALID. A prose log, exception string, unbound result row, intended cell, or malformed dispatch claim cannot establish INVALID evidence. The receipt must bind the exact defective frontier regular object itself. If that object is missing, symlinked, nonregular, resolution-failing, unexpectedly present, or storage-drifted, the receipt must instead bind the mandatory canonical controller gate observation derived from the normative table. protocol.json, r4_harness.py, and schemas.json never enter this rule after seal freeze because the potentially changed protocol/harness/schema cannot certify its own drift; the external fail-stop boundary aborts before this receipt path. evidence_paths never creates a cell, repairs a dispatch, broadens allowed runtime, or excuses later evidence.

failure_and_invalidation.cohort_invalid_propagation: A cohort INVALID class observed anywhere requires the canonical controller-invalid receipt, invalidates all three configurations and the comparison, preserves existing evidence, prohibits further subject calls and writes, and prevents pass/fail or relative-quality terminal claims. controller_invalid_close binds that receipt and emits every configuration terminal_status INVALID, including configurations whose earlier subject stages passed or failed.
failure_and_invalidation.protocol_change: Any change to protocol, template, schema, role contract, scorer, route, token or timeout policy, source or capsule bytes, fault selector, deterministic transform, controller, custody, rendering, binding, write, or close rule creates a new protocol revision. Rerun the earliest affected stage in all three configurations and every transitive consumer; never mix revision hashes.
failure_and_invalidation.artifact_change: Any actual artifact byte change invalidates every same-slot transitive consumer even when parsed JSON is semantically equivalent.
failure_and_invalidation.rescoring_only: A purely analytical presentation correction that changes no protocol, expected value, verdict rule, or artifact may create a new analysis version over preserved immutable evidence; otherwise it is a protocol change.

external_controller_self_hosting_fail_st.purpose: Prevent the candidate protocol, harness, or schemas from loading or executing changed bytes and then self-certifying their own drift.
external_controller_self_hosting_fail_st.prelaunch_seal_rule: All three remain ordinary required members of the exact 41-file launch-manifest inventory and must pass the same prelaunch hash/byte seal as every other immutable file.
external_controller_self_hosting_fail_st.external_authority: The orchestration controller outside r4_harness.py activates this boundary only after it has independently reopened canonical launch_manifest.json and detached custody, verified their exact identity, and frozen the three manifest rows' normalized paths, storage_sha256 values, and storage_bytes in controller state. The check does not import or execute r4_harness.py and does not load protocol.json or schemas.json to decide expected values.
external_controller_self_hosting_fail_st.check_algorithm: At every checkpoint, use external-controller filesystem primitives to lstat each lexical path and every existing ancestor without following links, require a regular nonlink file through nonlink ancestors, read exact raw storage bytes, and require byte count and SHA-256 to equal the frozen manifest row. Also require launch_manifest.json and detached custody still have the exact externally frozen payload/storage identity from activation. Any missing path, symlink, nonregular object, resolution/read error, byte-count mismatch, or SHA-256 mismatch fails the checkpoint. Current file claims, candidate parsers, receipt status, and harness output are never inputs to this decision.
external_controller_self_hosting_fail_st.pass_effect: Only an all-three exact match at the immediately applicable checkpoint permits that one invocation, dispatch, wait, read, acceptance, or storage action. A prior pass grants no later permission.
external_controller_self_hosting_fail_st.drift_effect: On the first failed checkpoint, do not invoke the harness or subject operation guarded by that checkpoint; discard without trusting any just-returned harness bytes; perform no further subject dispatch, wait, read, capture, scoring, deterministic transform, sandbox write, wave event, index, result manifest, controller observation, controller-invalid receipt, or cohort close in this attempt. An already running subject task may finish externally but its output is not read or credited.
external_controller_self_hosting_fail_st.external_terminal: The external orchestration controller marks the attempt ABORTED_EXTERNAL_SELF_HOSTING_DRIFT_NO_EMPIRICAL_CREDIT in its parent process/reporting state, names the mismatching sealed control and expected-versus-observed raw identity, and preserves already written evidence without asking the candidate harness to validate it. This external abort is not FIRST_ATTEMPT_FAIL, cohort INVALID certified by this protocol, normal W99 closure, empirical model evidence, or a model comparison.
external_controller_self_hosting_fail_st.credit_rule: Every subject/provider call already launched in the aborted attempt remains historical custody-only call activity and contributes zero empirical pass/fail, quality, audit, or comparative credit. No configuration or cohort terminal result may be inferred from it.
external_controller_self_hosting_fail_st.resume_rule: The aborted attempt is never resumed or internally repaired. Any later test requires a newly prepared and independently sealed candidate/attempt under separate authorization, with affected tests rerun; existing runtime bytes are not mixed into it.

Every slot root contains exactly result_manifest.json plus only nonempty evidence directories whose regular nonlink files are recognized by slot_recursive_file_patterns and bijectively justified by that slot's dispatched/reached evidence shapes. runtime_filesystem_allowlist.invalid_terminal_exact_shape: runs is a regular nonlink directory. runtime_filesystem_allowlist.recursive_enumeration_algorithm: At terminal validation lstat runs, every top-level child, and recursively every admitted directory without following links. For regular standard files reopen exact bytes through the appropriate semantic validator. A symlink/nonregular/missing expected path is terminalizable only through its exact normative observation and never grants traversal or other entries. Apply the same exact enumeration to sandboxes. The durable sibling preseal failure receipt outside the revision root is not part of runs, sandboxes, or the 41-file seal and is neither enumerated nor modified by this protocol.

controller_invalid_close.purpose: Executable fail-closed terminal path for W00 admission failure or W99 close failure when the normal sealed operational gate, passing launch currentness, passing close-source receipt, trusted wave index, or normal result manifests cannot be required.
controller_invalid_close.admission_exemption: This command is not a runtime-cell operational command and takes no wave dispatch receipt. It may run without passing sealed preflight and without a passing close-source receipt. It may do no render, subject call, score, transform, or sandbox write.

Missing, symlink, nonregular, resolution, unexpected-presence, or storage-drift defects are represented by and revalidated through the exact canonical runs/cohort/controller_invalid_observations/<wave_id>.json contract. The receipt must bind the observed seal, manifest, launch-source, close-source, wave, route, identity, or filesystem error rather than only an exception message.

controller_invalid_close.W99_historical_launch_recovery: Before dereferencing source_checks/launch.json, launch_manifest.json, detached custody, close.json, or an optional index, lstat the lexical path and every ancestor without following links. If an optional object is missing, a symlink, nonregular, or resolution-failing, do not open/resolve it; require the corresponding normative controller gate observation and continue the invalid-close path. Recover candidate historical launch payload hashes only from: (1) an intrinsically valid canonical launch receipt; (2) the exact nested launch_source_receipt.payload_sha256 in a canonical launch manifest whose detached payload/storage identity, schema, key order, exact 41 paths, configs/literals, and equality between its nested launch binding and its source_checks/launch.json inventory row validate, and whose immutable rows all match current storage except one exact non-self-referential row may instead be proven by the applicable canonical W99_LAUNCH_RECEIPT or STATIC_INVENTORY_ENTRY observation against that sealed row; and (3) launch_source_receipt_sha256 in an intrinsically valid canonical W10 dispatch whose protocol, W10 kind, null prior hash, exact all-three-active slot-by-stage cross-product, null task/thread fields, ordering, and status validate without trusting later events. protocol.json, r4_harness.py, and schemas.json are never observation exceptions here. Every available candidate must agree. A disagreement is BINDING INVALID and the exact conflicting regular objects are receipt-bound. Use the one agreed recovered hash to validate W10 and the remaining prefix and emit launch_source_receipt_sha256 even when the launch receipt path is defective. If no candidate survives, leave launch_source_receipt_sha256 null, treat W10 as no later than the invalid frontier rather than trusted prefix, require exact bound negative/defective evidence, and still permit INVALID terminalization. A defective close receipt is handled identically with W99_CLOSE_RECEIPT observation; close_source_observation_sha256 binds the exact canonical gate observation when no canonical close receipt payload exists.
controller_invalid_close.postlaunch_static_inventory_drift_route: This normal W99 internal route applies only to an immutable_inventory member other than protocol.json, r4_harness.py, and schemas.json. When operational sealed preflight detects drift of one such non-self-referential member after W10 dispatch eligibility began, first lstat the launch manifest, detached custody, and target without following links. Intrinsically validate the manifest and detached payload/storage identity, exact schema/key order/literals, exact 41-row sorted inventory, and select the target's sealed storage_sha256/storage_bytes; do not require the current target to match. Derive invalid wave as the currently stored intrinsically valid dispatch wave, otherwise the next registered wave immediately after the maximal trustworthy completed prefix, or W99 after W90. Emit and apply_patch-store exactly runs/cohort/controller_invalid_observations/<invalid-wave>.json with gate_code STATIC_INVENTORY_ENTRY, the exact target path, expectation MATCH_BOUND_STORAGE from that sealed row, current no-follow storage identity, defect_kind STORAGE_DRIFT, and invalid_class limited to SEAL_DRIFT, CUSTODY, or FILESYSTEM. Then store the same-wave controller-invalid receipt with slot and stage both null and evidence_paths binding that observation. No task, cell, transform, write, later dispatch, or retry may occur after detection. The drifted static file is preserved outside runs as observed evidence; it receives no runtime role and evidence_paths grants nothing else. controller_invalid_close runs in W99 terminal mode, validates the trustworthy completed prefix before this frontier, revalidates the observation against the same sealed row, and emits INVALID. For historical launch recovery, the sealed manifest remains trustworthy when detached identity, the launch binding, and every immutable row other than this exact non-self-referential observation target validate; the target's sealed row plus the canonical observation replaces only its current-byte equality check. If target is protocol.json, r4_harness.py, or schemas.json, or if manifest/detached custody is defective, this route is unavailable; self-hosting control drift uses external_controller_self_hosting_fail_stop and never enters W99 internal closure.
controller_invalid_close.maximal_trustworthy_prefix_algorithm: Starting at W10 and without trusting cohort_wave_index.json, examine waves in fixed order. A wave is appended to the trustworthy completed prefix only after its dispatch and completion plus every reservation, creation metadata, attempt-start, post-task metadata, packet, capture, ordinary or failure receipt, deterministic artifact, S80 custody record, route/identity binding, status derivation, and predecessor hash chain have passed the same full semantic validators used by normal wave-check. Merely parsing canonical JSON or reading completion.status is never sufficient. A fully valid completion whose status is INVALID and binds the exact canonical controller-invalid receipt may be appended as the final trustworthy wave. At the first missing, malformed, or semantically invalid required event or cell artifact, stop before that wave; do not append either event or infer trust from its claimed status. That wave is the invalid frontier and the defective regular evidence object, or the canonical gate observation representing a negative/nonregular defect, must be bound by the controller-invalid receipt so controller_invalid_close can terminalize the defect without treating it as part of the trustworthy prefix.
controller_invalid_close.invalid_frontier_evidence: The controller-invalid receipt wave_id must equal W00, W99, the final trustworthy wave whose fully valid completion is INVALID, or the first runtime invalid-frontier wave immediately after the trustworthy prefix. A frontier dispatch grants cells only after full intrinsic validation proves canonical storage/schema, exact frontier wave/kind, correct prior-completion and recovered launch bindings, and the complete active-slot by registered-stage cross-product. Only then may slot/stage name one exact dispatch item. A missing, nonregular, malformed, semantically invalid, partial, extra, reordered, wrong-stage, wrong-active-slot, or wrong-wave dispatch grants zero cells and requires null slot/stage. The receipt binds the exact defective regular frontier object; a missing/nonregular/symlink/resolution/unexpected-presence/storage-drift object requires the exact normative controller gate observation. Then enumerate the complete standard roots. Receipt evidence_paths is not an activity allowlist: no listed path may excuse a later-wave event, a cell absent from the frontier dispatch, a stopped-slot later cell, a post-invalid task/call/write, an S80 target not justified by a fully validated PASS S80 in the trustworthy prefix, or a normal result/close artifact. At the invalid frontier, only the defective event or cell evidence, pre-invalid predecessors, cells already authorized by the immutable frontier dispatch, the canonical gate observation, the canonical invalid receipt, an optional untrusted index bound as the defect, and controller_invalid_close itself may exist; each is still semantically classified and validated to the extent possible. Every event or cell path in a wave after the frontier is rejected even if named by evidence_paths. Unknown, duplicate-alias, symlink, nonregular, or unclassified runtime entries are CUSTODY INVALID and cannot broaden the frontier.
